item.title: Riley discusses Valley construction projects
item.description: Mayor Riley outlines a busy 2026 for Valley, with new subdivisions, a school site, businesses and major road work planned as the city builds on stronger finances.

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - John Tures: Republicans Are Now Joining Democrats In Recognizing That ICE Has Gone Too Far

item.title: Riverkeeper talks efforts to keep the Chattahoochee clean
item.description: Chattahoochee Riverkeeper details clean-up gains, lawsuits and intensive water monitoring that have helped make the river far cleaner than in the 1960s despite Atlanta’s growth.

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - L. Michelle Moore: Mutual Aid
item.description: Mutual aid among utilities is a longstanding and powerful tradition, and the crews and individual lineworkers who roll trucks in the most extreme weather to get the power back on are everyday heroes. As our hometowns languish in the deep freeze, we each have an important opportunity to provide mutual aid, too. item.title: Springwood varsity teams drop over 70 points on Senior Night
item.description: Wildcat basketball is continuing its tear on the season. On Friday, the Springwood varsity basketball teams came up big at home against Evangel Christian. The girls first did it in style with a 73-37 victory, followed by the boys’ equally dominating 74-52 win.

item.title: Lanett loses to Troup in nail-biter on Senior Night
item.description: On Lanett’s Senior Night, both Panther teams fell in nail-biters to Troup, 60-58 and 54-52.

item.title: State Elections Tuesday
item.description: Voters in House District 38 head to the polls Feb. 3 to choose between Hazel Floyd and Kristin Nelson in a special election to finish former Rep. Debbie Wood’s term; polls open 7 a.m.–7 p.m.

item.title: Unite awarded $3.9M grant to launch civic institute at HBCUs
item.description: LaFayette nonprofit Unite won a $3.9M federal grant to launch a national HBCU Civil Discourse & Freedom Institute, expanding civic education and training across campuses.

item.title: West Point woman receives new heating unit from Fuller Center
item.description: After weeks with little heat, a 92-year-old West Point woman gets a new heating unit through the Fuller Center’s Greater Blessings program.

item.title: A Simple Guide to What Police Are Allowed to Do
item.description: Police make sure that laws are followed, keep the peace, and keep people safe. The law gives them authority, but it also limits what they can do.
